discover.output: Reconnaissance complete for window 2026-10-10..2026-10-17. Inspected activity-summary (apps/windows), OCR searches for tracker.csv, scan-04xx, Atlas, Beacon, Climbers. Found two distinct, evidenced candidate jobs and handed both to workflow-deepen: (1) receipt/contract scan intake & filing into tracker.csv with duplicate/over-threshold/missing-date flags (TextEdit+Preview+Finder, 2026-10-16); (2) emailed project document filing into Projects/<Name> folder + reply confirmation, observed twice with different senders/projects (Beacon w/ Priya Shah 10-15, Atlas w/ Alex Moreau 10-16), suggesting a generalizable habit. Checked Discord 'Weekend Climbers' activity - casual personal chat (pizza/weather banter), not a work job. Browsing of sourdough/keyboards/trains/weather pages appears to be personal leisure research with no actionable outcome, not included as a job. No existing catalog workflows to compare against (catalogRevision 0, empty workflows list). Coverage limitation: did not exhaustively replay every frame; relied on representative OCR snapshots per window/app. Did not verify destination folder of renamed receipt scans (tracker.csv only, no Finder move observed) - flagged as open question for deepen.

maintain.output: Inspected workflow_workspace context (revision 1, catalogRevision 0): saved workflows list is empty, no drafts assigned to workflow-maintain, researchNotes empty. There is nothing in the existing catalog to investigate, correct, enrich, or re-time. Also reviewed activity-summary for the cycle window (2026-10-10 to 2026-10-17): activity is mostly personal browsing (sourdough baking, keyboards, night trains, weather, climbing Discord) plus a tracker.csv in TextEdit and Finder paperwork inbox — no clear recurring/repeated job matching an existing workflow since none exist yet. Recommend workflow-discover populate the catalog first; workflow-maintain has nothing to act on until then.

workflows.title: Receipt and contract scan intake: inspect, classify, and log to tracker.csv
workflows.trigger: New scanned receipt or contract PDFs appear in /Users/<redacted>/Documents/Paperwork/Inbox (observed scans scan-0414.pdf through scan-0421.pdf present 2026-10-16).
workflows.outcome: tracker.csv is updated with one row per scan, recording a proposed renamed filename, date, amount, type, status (filed/duplicate/review needed), and notes explaining any flag (e.g. 'over 500', 'missing date', 'same as <other file>'). No evidence was found that files are actually renamed or moved on disk, or that flagged rows receive further action.
variations: Some scans lack a readable date and are logged with 'UNKNOWN-DATE' placeholder and a 'missing date' note (scan-0415).
Some scans are recognized as duplicates of an already-filed item and logged with status 'duplicate' instead of a new filename (scan-0417, duplicate of scan-0412).
Amounts over 500 are flagged status 'review needed' with a note citing the threshold (scan-0418, 780.00, 'over 500').
At least one item's type was inferred from an external client list when the document itself didn't state it (scan-0420, 'type from client list').
limitations: Only the tracker.csv end-state and two Preview scan sessions (scan-0420 ~10:10-10:11Z, scan-0421 ~11:27-11:28Z) were directly re-verified; earlier scans in the batch (0414-0419) we
No direct evidence of the physical file rename/move step was found despite searching; the workflow as published covers only the inspect-classify-log portion.
No ordered capture example covers every step. These references do not establish one end-to-end occurrence.
Only one captured day supports this candidate; repetition is not established.

workflows.title: File emailed project document into matching Projects folder and reply to confirm
workflows.trigger: A colleague emails an updated project document as a PDF attachment, sometimes with an explicit filing instruction (e.g. Alex Moreau: 'Timeline for Atlas attached, same place as the brief please').
workflows.outcome: The document is saved into the correct project folder next to prior documents for that project (older versions/documents are not deleted or archived, they simply coexist), and the sender receives a brief reply confirming the filing location.
variations: Beacon instance: new version (v2) of an existing document (budget) saved alongside v1, both present in folder afterward.
Atlas instance: a new distinct document (timeline) saved alongside an existing different document (project brief) in the same project folder, prompted by sender's explicit instruct
limitations: Only two instances were observed within this one-week window; recurrence/cadence beyond that is unconfirmed.
Did not verify whether this habit holds for non-PDF attachments or other project folders not seen this week.
No ordered capture example covers every step. These references do not establish one end-to-end occurrence.
